claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films have an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
These as-deposited films exhibit a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
A moderate post-deposition anneal below the secondary-phase formation temperature will relieve internal strain.
The anneal will modify grain-boundary characteristics.
Annealing-induced strain relief will rebalance the film's elastic-energy landscape.
Changes in residual stress and grain-boundary features will alter nucleation kinetics of the magnetostructural transition.
Changes in residual stress and grain-boundary features will alter propagation kinetics of the magnetostructural transition.
The altered transition kinetics will broaden the magnetocaloric transition.
The altered transition kinetics will reduce hysteresis during low-applied-field cooling cycles.
Annealing will cause a slight, predictable shift in transition temperature.
Annealing within the proposed window will not introduce unwanted secondary phases.
The predicted effects apply only in a narrow annealing-temperature window that relieves strain without causing secondary-phase formation or significant compositional change.
The predicted effects should be robust among films made under similar deposition conditions.
Bulk and ribbon observations suggest a relationship between local strain and transition sharpness.
As-deposited films have limited heat-exchange performance.
The comparison should use annealed and unannealed films produced by the same deposition process and tested under identical low-field cycles.

contradictions.description: The boundary restricts the hypothesis to anneals below secondary-phase formation, but the falsification rule treats detection of secondary phases as falsifying the governing mechanism. Such detection could instead show that the intervention fell outside the stated validity window.
